title: Objectwise K-flat replacements in strict diagram categories
statement:
Let $J$ be a small category, let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be small sites, and let $\mathcal O,\mathcal O'$ be sheaves of commutative rings on them. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ for the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A complex of strict $J$-diagrams means a cochain complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$; evaluation at $j$ gives a cochain complex $M(j)$ of sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Quasi-isomorphisms in this diagram category are the maps whose evaluations induce isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

For every such complex $M$, there is a morphism $P\to M$ of strict diagrams of complexes, termwise surjective and a quasi-isomorphism at every $j$, such that each $P(j)$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and every term $P(j)^q$ is flat, meaning that tensoring with it is exact on sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules.

Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi (an adjoint pair $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits), together with a ring homomorphism $c:u^{-1}\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$. Define module pullback termwise by $u^*F=u^{-1}F\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $P\to Q$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism of strict diagram complexes and every $P(j),Q(j)$ is K-flat with flat terms, then $u^*P\to u^*Q$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism. The replacements and maps here are in the strict diagram category, not a choice of unrelated replacements in each derived category.

source.place: Tags 077J (sites-cohomology-lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero) and 0G7E (sites-cohomology-lemma-pullback-K-flat), applied to the small diagram site; the diagram interpretation is an agent extension of these constructions. Quasi-isomorphism invariance is the cone argument of Tag 06YY (sites-cohomology-lemma-derived-base-change), using the acyclic K-flat case in the proof of Tag 0G7E; Tag 0G7E itself states preservation of K-flatness, rather than quasi-isomorphism invariance.

proof.text: Reuse the proved functorial-flat-cover and exact integer-colimit infrastructure of lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Reduce the cover to preserve zero morphisms, and use the existing left-resolution functor on all cochain complexes. Compose the entire strict diagram M with this one functor. Its natural augmentation gives a morphism of strict diagrams; the resolution API proves each component is a quasi-isomorphism. The colimit presentation proves flatness of every term, and kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj proves categorical K-flatness of each component. No separate objectwise choices of resolutions or lifts of transition maps are made.

Transpose the resolution and target to complexes in the diagram category. The same functorial flat cover gives covers Q_i of every target diagram in degree i. Form D^i=Q_i direct-sum Q_(i-1), with differential first projection followed by the next second inclusion. The reverse second-to-first map is a contracting homotopy. The maps [q_i, q_(i-1) followed by the target differential] define D to M, epimorphic in each degree. Add D and this map to the resolution and its augmentation. The explicit projection and inclusion form a homotopy equivalence; its inclusion followed by the new augmentation is the old augmentation. All disk, chain-map, contraction and factorization equations are proved in the private epicification lemma. This is the contractible-disk step of the existing resolution construction, generalized to the isomorphism-invariant class of objectwise flat diagrams.

Evaluation preserves homotopies, finite biproducts and epimorphisms. Transfer categorical K-flatness along the evaluated homotopy equivalence. Apply tensor-right to the quasi-isomorphism from zero to any acyclic complex to recover IsAcyclicTensorKFlat. Objectwise categorical flatness supplies the required exact tensor-right predicate. The factorization of the old augmentation through the homotopy equivalence and new augmentation gives the new quasi-isomorphism by two-out-of-three. These deductions are written explicitly in Lean using the homotopy-category and evaluation APIs.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-supplied-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback to the given ringed-topos morphism. It produces an additive left adjoint F to the supplied module direct image and proves that termwise F preserves quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat complexes. Both F and the given E are left adjoint to that same functor. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives F isomorphic to E; its image on complexes and its naturality square give an isomorphism of arrows for every component of alpha. Quasi-isomorphism invariance under arrow isomorphisms transfers the result from F to E. The maps of the resulting strict diagram are the whiskered natural transformation already in the conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem exists_diagram_isKFlatResolution {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (T : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf T CommRingCat.{u}) {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] (M : J ⥤ CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose T (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ) : ∃ (P : J ⥤ CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose T (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R)) ℤ) (p : P ⟶ M), (∀ j : J, (P.obj j).IsAcyclicTensorKFlat) ∧ (∀ (j : J) (q : ℤ), SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((P.obj j).X q)) ∧ (∀ j : J, QuasiIso (p.app j)) ∧ (∀ (j : J) (q : ℤ), Epi ((p.app j).f q))
lean.note: The two declarations render the replacement and pullback-invariance clauses respectively. Strict diagrams are functors into cochain complexes. Pullback is specified, uniquely up to natural isomorphism, as an additive left adjoint to the existing induced module direct image (Stacks 03D7).
